items.question: What is ALTIX Exchange?
items.answer: ALTIX Exchange is a Singapore-based technology and services company serving litigation finance and global asset recovery. It prepares selected legal and recovery matters for professional funding through structured assessment, evidence organization, financial analysis, collectability work, investor materials and administration.

items.question: What services does ALTIX provide?
items.answer: ALTIX provides case screening, Case Readiness, evidence organization, financial and collectability analysis, investment-material preparation, controlled access to suitable funding participants and post-closing administration where agreed.

items.question: Is ALTIX a law firm?
items.answer: ALTIX is described in its current business plan as a technology and services company. Independent legal professionals remain responsible for legal advice, legal strategy and professional judgment. Confirm this final wording with Singapore counsel before production launch.

items.question: Does ALTIX fund every case directly?
items.answer: No. Depending on the matter, funding may be considered by specialist funders, professional investors, case-specific vehicles or other eligible capital providers. Submission does not guarantee acceptance or funding.

items.question: Who can access funding opportunities?
items.answer: Access is restricted according to investor eligibility, product structure, jurisdiction, KYC/AML requirements and applicable law. ALTIX’s current business plan contemplates an initial private model for professional, institutional and eligible investors rather than unrestricted public access.

items.question: Is public token trading live on ALTIX?
items.answer: No. ALTIX’s current business plan treats public token trading and an open secondary market as future products rather than current base-launch services. Any future transfer functionality will require legal, regulatory, tax and product review.

items.question: Does ALTIX guarantee returns or recoveries?
items.answer: No. Legal and recovery outcomes are uncertain. Matters can lose, take longer than expected, recover less than anticipated or result in total investment loss.

items.question: How does ALTIX assess matters?
items.answer: ALTIX considers claimant authority, legal merit, evidence, damages, limitation, budget, duration, adverse costs, defendant quality, collectability, enforcement, integrity, investor terms and legal structure. Independent legal advice remains necessary.

items.question: Where is ALTIX based?
items.answer: ALTIX is described in its current business plan as Singapore-based. Add the verified legal entity name, UEN and registered office here after checking the current company record.

data.title: What Is Litigation Finance? A Practical Guide for Businesses
data.excerpt: Litigation finance is a structure in which external capital can support the costs of pursuing a legal claim, subject to the relevant agreement and jurisdiction.

children.text: A claimant may have a legally credible claim but still face legal fees, expert costs, adverse-cost exposure or enforcement expenditure that it prefers not to carry entirely on its own balance sheet. Litigation finance can transfer part of that cost and risk to an external capital provider.

Professional funding review typically considers legal merit, evidence, damages, budget, expected duration, adverse costs, defendant quality, collectability, enforcement and the economic terms of the proposed funding.
A funder-ready matter is more than a legal memorandum. It needs a coherent chronology, evidence index, supported damages, realistic budget and a credible route from legal success to actual recovery.
ALTIX helps organize selected legal and recovery matters into a more consistent format for professional review and may coordinate access to suitable funding participants.

data.title: Legal Merit Is Not Enough: Why Collectability Matters
data.excerpt: A claim can be legally strong and economically weak if a successful judgment cannot realistically be converted into recovery.

children.text: Judgment and recovery are different questions
Underwriting a legal asset requires both a view on legal success and a view on what can actually be collected after settlement or judgment.
Relevant factors include defendant solvency, insurance, asset location, ownership structure, enforcement venues, competing creditors, freezing options and likely cost of enforcement.
Early collectability work can prevent capital from being committed to matters where the headline damages are disconnected from realistic recovery.
International recovery can involve several legal systems, disclosure tools, insolvency processes and asset classes. Specialist legal and forensic input may therefore be required.

sections.title: Judgment and recovery are different questions
sections.body: Underwriting a legal asset requires both a view on legal success and a view on what can actually be collected after settlement or judgment.

sections.title: What collectability review may consider
sections.body: Relevant factors include defendant solvency, insurance, asset location, ownership structure, enforcement venues, competing creditors, freezing options and likely cost of enforcement.

sections.title: Why this belongs before funding

data.title: What Makes a Legal Claim Suitable for Funding?
data.excerpt: Funding suitability depends on a combination of legal merit, evidence, economics, collectability, duration, integrity and structure.

children.text: Legal merit is the starting point
Independent legal review should identify the cause of action, standing, likely defences, jurisdiction, limitation and the strength of the available evidence.
Funders compare realistic recoverable value with the litigation budget, expected duration, risk and proposed return structure.
A strong judgment has limited economic value if the defendant lacks assets, insurance or an enforceable recovery route.
Authority, KYC/AML, sanctions, conflicts, document authenticity and credible counterparties are part of a professional funding process.
ALTIX Case Readiness is intended to identify these issues early and organize a suitable matter before professional capital is approached.
